root_idea.summary: The root centers on rest, stillness, and cessation, with a closely related branch of cutting off or interrupting.
root_idea.development: The evidence connects easy, quiet movement and repose with cessation, sleep, shaving or removing hair, and states of completion or softening. The naming of the Sabbath is variously explained through cessation of work or completion of creation, while another analysis foregrounds cutting off.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form سَبَتَ.
Displayed as the Quranic verbal noun سُبَات.
Displayed under the normalized noun citation form سَبْت.

senses.definition: To enter upon or observe the Sabbath, refraining from work.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic usage is in the imperfect plural construction describing people who observed or entered upon the Sabbath and ceased their ordinary labor.

senses.definition: Rest or repose, especially sleep as a period of rest.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the construction وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا, describing sleep as restorative repose.

senses.definition: A cutting off or interruption of activity, sensation, and motion.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic sleep construction, this describes sleep as cutting a person off from work, sensation, and ordinary movement.

senses.definition: A death-like cessation of bodily motion and sensation, interpreted in one Quranic explanation as death.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an interpretation of سُبَاتًا in the sleep passage rather than a separate Quranic object or event.

senses.definition: The Sabbath: the designated day of cessation from work, together with its observance.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the Sabbath day in expressions such as يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ and of the institution whose observance required cessation from work.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rest; cease from work; become quiet, still, or motionless; and, by extension, to sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: General Classical Arabic verbal usage, distinct from the Quranic specialized use of observing the Sabbath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rest, quietness, stillness, or freedom from motion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal usage of سَبْتٌ as a state of repose or stillness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to go at the pace called سَبْتٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal use describing a camel’s manner of going.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rapid pace or outstripping in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a pace exceeding ordinary running, especially in descriptions of camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confusion or perplexity that leaves a person unable to see the right course, with consequent silence or downcast gaze.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or nominal application to a person in a state of perplexity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut, sever, intercept, interrupt, or bring to an end, literally or figuratively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With a neck or head, the construction means to decapitate; with a morsel and the throat, it means to obstruct or stop the passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shave the head or remove the hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the head or hair as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To let the hair down after it has been twisted or plaited.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional hair-grooming usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be affected by sleep-like stupor, swoon, or sick prostration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, especially one who appears asleep or has closed eyes through illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic extension of the passive verbal state associated with cessation and sleep-like stillness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a serpent, to become silent or lower its head and eyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a serpent’s subdued or motionless posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To induce sleep-like torpor, or to torpify and benumb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a drug or medicinal substance producing numbness or stupor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cut off, interrupted, stopped, ended, or to cease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form VII usage describing an activity or process that comes to an end.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become long or extended, together with softness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied, for example, to an elongated and soft or gently extended countenance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a hide, to become soft through tanning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the result of the tanning process.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dates, to become ripe throughout and soft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when ripeness has pervaded the date completely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A week, or a period or span of time, whether short or long.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can denote the interval from one Sabbath to the next, a period of time, or time in general; the idiom ابنا سبت refers to the night and day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift or excellent horse that runs much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a horse distinguished by speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bold, daring boy or young man of bad disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal epithet combining boldness with an ill nature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cunning, intelligent, and discerning man, excellent in judgment; also one who is silent or downcast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a person characterized by intelligence, craft, or subdued silence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who sleeps much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal description derived from كثرة السبات.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant resembling marsh-mallow, reportedly used for tanning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant-name distinct from the Sabbath noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hide or skin, especially an ox-hide, that has been tanned, including hide tanned with qaraz.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to the hide whether or not tanned in every usage, but especially to soft tanned ox-hide.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sandals made from such tanned hides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional metonymic use of the leather term for sandals lacking hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dill or a similar well-known herb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized plant name, distinct from the native lexical branches of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Goats collectively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bare or treeless desert or tract of land, as though shorn of its vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of barren land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having spreading or expanded ears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine epithet applied to an animal with ears of this shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who fasts alone on the Sabbath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective describing a person’s distinctive Sabbath observance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foolish, stupid, or of little sense; confused and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal epithet for intellectual deficiency or perplexity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that continually goes at a quick pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a camel’s sustained gait.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bold or daring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applicable to a person or animal; the feminine form is separately used with a feminine ending.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leopard, lion, or beast of prey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-name or epithet associated with boldness and daring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sharp-tongued or vehemently clamorous woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine application describing a woman’s loud or foul-tongued speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Motionless or not moving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial description of a person or thing remaining still.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Entering upon or observing the Sabbath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle refers correctly to entering upon the observance of the Sabbath, rather than merely entering a calendar day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by sleep-like stupor or swoon, or prostrated like a sleeping sick person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to someone whose eyes are generally closed through stupor or illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confounded or perplexed and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or psychological application of the passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic passive-participial use associated with complete cessation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cut off, as a head that has been severed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression رَأْسٌ مَسْبُوتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dates, ripe throughout and soft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial description of dates whose ripeness has fully pervaded them.
